title: StrongGrowthHessianLipschitz.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a C² real-valued function; convexity is not required. The initial objective gap satisfies f(x0)−inf f≤Δ.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns g(x,ξ) using fresh IID randomness, with E[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x). Only gradient samples are available; function values and Hessians are not supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StrongGrowthHessianLipschitz.lean: spec.admissible, oracle answer and unbiasedness clauses; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID

distinctive_assumptions.label: relative_error
distinctive_assumptions.details: Unbiased multiplicative second-moment noise: E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖²≤(κ−1)‖∇f(x)‖², κ≥1. Equivalently E‖g(x,ξ)‖²≤κ‖∇f(x)‖²; this is a mean-square strong-growth condition, not a samplewise relative-error bound.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Globally L-Lipschitz gradient and ρ-Lipschitz Hessian in operator norm. Public parameters include L>0, ρ>0, κ≥1, Δ≥0, ε>0 and x0, with 4^8 ρε≤L². The objective and gradient-sampling distribution are hidden.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: A measurable output X with integrable gradient norm must satisfy E‖∇f(X)‖≤ε.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over algorithm randomness and IID oracle randomness, under a fixed cap on total stochastic-gradient calls.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: An established smooth nonconvex stationarity formulation with Lipschitz Hessian and the standard unbiased strong-growth stochastic-gradient model.

descriptionHtml:
Stationarity Under Strong Growth

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex, twice continuously differentiable function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. Its gradient and Hessian are Lipschitz with constants L>0 and ρ>0, and a given point x0∈E satisfies f(x0)−infx∈Ef(x)≤Δ, where Δ≥0. The oracle returns unbiased stochastic gradients with independent, identically distributed samples and mean squared error at most (κ−1)∥∇f(x)∥2, where κ≥1. The goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with E∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, where ε>0 satisfies 48ρε≤L2.

The optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, L, ρ, κ, Δ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Gradient and Hessian regularity). The function f belongs to C2(E;R), and, for all x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤ρ∥x−y∥. Here ∇2f(x):E→E is the derivative of the gradient.

Assumption 2 (Initial objective gap). The given point x0 satisfies f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ,x∈E.

Assumption 3 (Strong-growth stochastic oracle). There is a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the random vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable for ξ∼ν, with Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤(κ−1)∥∇f(x)∥2. The samples (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law ν under a joint probability law Q on ΩN. At the kth query x∈E, the oracle returns g(x,ξk). Algorithm randomness is independent of this sample sequence.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its gradient norm must be integrable, and it must satisfy EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f∈C2 has L-Lipschitz gradient, ρ-Lipschitz Hessian, and f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ for every x. The jointly measurable IID oracle is unbiased with integrable gradients and squared errors satisfying E∥g(x)−∇f(x)∥2≤(κ−1)∥∇f(x)∥2. Here L,ρ,ε>0, κ≥1, Δ≥0, and 48ρε≤L2. Target: ∫∥∇f(out(ξ))∥dP(ξ)≤ε, for the constructed restarted AGD’s validated candidate; the setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.StrongGrowthHessianLipschitz

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  κ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.ρ ∧ 1 ≤ q.κ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧ 4 ^ 8 * q.ρ * q.ε ≤ q.L ^ 2
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (P0 : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (P0 : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    ContDiff ℝ 2 f ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) y‖ ≤ q.ρ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x, f q.x0 - f x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(P0 : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤ (q.κ - 1) * ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.StrongGrowthHessianLipschitz
